body:
When the unbroken circle cannot be entered, the seer rests in autonomy-power and experiences undivided Bhairava-immersion. The teaching: all things are mere reflections in the sky of awareness — mirror, taste, smell, touch, echo. Reflections are non-primary (no unseen effects) yet not non-existent. The universe stands to the Lord's light the same way. The "no source-image?" objection is dissolved: the cause is the Lord's power = autonomy, which holds the universe's reflection; graspinglessness would be inertness. Grasping is non-conventional, resonance-pregnant, coextensive with the power-multitude. Three chief powers (unsurpassed/will/unfolding) = grasping-triads a-i-u / ā-ī-ū; whole power-expanse enacted thence. Sun-triad (light-portion) vs moon-triad (rest-bliss) while action absent; action entering will/sovereignty → ra/la sounds (light-pillar), unmanifest (else creation, not will). Four neuters ṛṝḷḹ bearing both shadows.

The passage moves in four steps, each deepening the seeing. First, the reflection doctrine: all things = mere reflections in awareness-sky (six similes: mirror, taste in tooth-water, smell in nose, couple's touch, thorn-spear touch, echo in sky); reflections are non-primary (no unseen effects like disease-cure) yet not non-existent (body-dusting, emission are seen); the universe stands to the Lord's light exactly so. Second, the "no source-image?" objection dissolved: cause = Lord's power = autonomy (graspinglessness → inertness; grasping non-conventional, resonance-pregnant, coextensive with power-multitude). The grasping is not a label stuck on; it comes with being conscious the way resonance comes with a bell. Third, three chief powers = anuttara/icchā/unmeṣa = grasping-triads a-i-u / ā-ī-ū; whole power-expanse enacted thence; sun-triad (light-portion, sūryātmaka) vs moon-triad (rest-bliss, somātmaka) while action absent. Fourth, action entering will/sovereignty → ra/la sounds (light-pillar, ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt), unmanifest (else creation, not will); four neuters ṛṝḷḹ bearing both shadows.
terms: pratibimba (reflection), āmarśa (grasping, non-conventional), anuttara (unsurpassed), parāmarśa (grasping-triad), prakāśa (light), viśrānti (rest), ra/la (light-pillar sounds), anuttara/icchā/unmeṣa (three chief powers).
see_also: A02 (anupāya), A04 (śākta), essay0 Q4 ("How do I see this?"), spans TS3.1–3.13.
function: Establishes the śāmbhava upāya (seeing) and the phoneme-womb doctrine: reflections → grasping → powers → phonemes.
local_context: A02 (anupāya) precedes; A03 teaches seeing via reflection; A04 (śākta) follows.
boundary: Similes assume everyday assent (mild, external). Letter-derivations assume āgamic phonology (heavy external dependency).

body:
When Unsurpassed and Bliss pour into the wills, two letters sound: e, oṃ. Clashing back together, two more: ai, au — and that foursome is action-power itself. When every effect is about to rest back in the Unsurpassed, it waits first as pure sensing, sheer light, a point: aṃ. Then, right there, the Unsurpassed breathes out: aḥ. Sixteen graspings, all seed. Out of seed, the consonants, the womb. Letter-classes assigned: ka/ca/ṭa/ta/pa by five powers; ya-ra-la from three wills; va from unfolding; śa-ṣa-sa from three wills; ha from emission; kṣa from womb-union. So the Lord, unsurpassed, wears Kuleśvara's shape. His is one clan-emission-power: from bliss-nature throbbing all the way out to creation's edge, graspings turn into outer principles. The emission is three: stopping mind (atom's way), waking mind (power's way), dissolving mind (Śambhu's way) — emission itself is how the Lord worlds the world. Grasped whole, he is one, seed-and-womb; grasped in parts, owner and owned. Counts: eight graspings apart with wheel-lords = nine; one grasping leading = fifty; possible divisions = eighty-one; really six graspings becoming twelve nourish the Lord's power-fullness; as powers, those goddesses spell Kālī. Pure graspings in pure knowledge take a half-other shape (vidyā/avidyā-lords via slight Māyā-contraction); in Māyā they splinter into Māyā-letters, usable through paśyantī/madhyamā/vaikharī down to outer principles; seen as body-scheme and re-ensouled by pure graspings, even fallen letters turn potent, giving enjoyment and liberation. Who sees the self this way — nothing but rest in all graspings, with every principle, being, and world mirrored in it — thought-free, in Śambhu's immersion, is free while living. And here too: no mantra strings attached.

The passage is a continuous derivation in six movements. (a) Phoneme emanation: when Unsurpassed and Bliss pour into the wills, two letters sound (e, oṃ); clashing back, two more (ai, au) — that foursome is action-power itself; when every effect rests back in the Unsurpassed, it waits first as pure sensing, sheer light, a point (aṃ); then the Unsurpassed breathes out (aḥ): sixteen graspings, all seed. (b) Letter-class assignment: out of seed, the consonants, the womb; ka/ca/ṭa/ta/pa by five powers; ya-ra-la from three wills; va from unfolding; śa-ṣa-sa from three wills; ha from emission; kṣa from womb-union — so the Lord, unsurpassed, wears Kuleśvara's shape. (c) One clan-emission-power: from bliss-nature throbbing all the way out to creation's edge, graspings turn into outer principles; emission threefold (āṇava/śākta/śāmbhava = mind-rest/awakening/dissolution) — emission itself is how the Lord worlds the world. (d) The numbers: grasped whole, he is one (seed-and-womb); grasped in parts, owner and owned; eight graspings apart with wheel-lords = nine; one grasping leading = fifty; possible divisions = eighty-one; really six graspings becoming twelve nourish the Lord's power-fullness; as powers, those goddesses spell Kālī. (e) Pure vs. fallen: pure graspings in pure knowledge take a half-other shape (vidyā/avidyā-lords via slight Māyā-contraction); in Māyā they splinter into Māyā-letters, usable through paśyantī/madhyamā/vaikharī down to outer principles; seen as body-scheme and re-ensouled by pure graspings, even fallen letters turn potent, giving enjoyment and liberation. (f) Jīvanmukti close: who sees the self this way — nothing but rest in all graspings, with every principle, being, and world mirrored in it — thought-free, in Śambhu's immersion, is free while living; no mantra strings attached.
terms: visarga (emission), bīja (seed), yoni (womb), Kuleśvara, āṇava/śākta/śāmbhava (three emissions), Kālī (etymology), vidyā/avidyā (knowing/unknowing lords), paśyantī/madhyamā/vaikharī (speech levels), jīvanmukti (living liberation).
see_also: A02 (anupāya), A04 (śākta), essay0 Q4, spans TS3.14–3.34.
function: Derivation map: grasping → letter → tattva → world; revivification restores power to fallen letters; jīvanmukti close.
local_context: P1 established reflection + first phoneme sets; P2 completes the derivation.
boundary: Letter-derivations assume āgamic phonology (heavy external-knowledge dependency). The "some say" (kecit) color-view (3.38) is uncjudicated.
